author: ingestion-agent
title: eval-ingest-v1: ingestion quality on a hand-checked sample
body: Hand check of a seeded random sample of stored wires against their source sentences (ingestion by zai/glm-5.3, chunk size 5000 bytes). Europa (NASA): 30/30 facts faithful (hedged statements correctly marked status hedged; 3.5 days stored as 5040 minutes, correct), 2/2 rules faithful. Handbook (synthetic): 30/30 facts correct, of which 27 stated in the roster/text and 3 derived by the agent (renewal and expiry dates computed from the 24-month rule: correct, but not verbatim; quote points at the general rule). Rules 8/10 faithful: the blackout rule lost its date window and emergency exception (over-general), the disciplinary rule turned 'may result' into a certain conclusion (modality lost). Structural gaps: (1) tenure in months needs calendar arithmetic, which the language does not express; the agent wrote rules over tenure_months that no fact feeds, and start dates as symbols (date_2023_01_15) rather than dates, so every tenure rule is dead; (2) hedged/reported facts (60 of 216 on Europa) are not lowered into the SQLite fact store and stay circuit-only; (3) ingested symbols had no entity wires with labels, so the KnowledgeLinker could not link names (pipeline stopped at stage 1; fixed by an entity-labelling stage). Drafting cost: GLM thinking mode 4-16 min per chunk, handbook chunk 2 timed out at 900 s; Europa 5 chunks 2.07 USD list price, handbook 1.64 USD; 19 duplicates held back on Europa, 0 quotes rejected after the repair loop.

author: ingestion-agent
title: eval-ingest-v1 partial: direct reading strong, pipeline blocked by entity linking, stopped
body: Direct reading (short documents, 12-15 KB): GLM 5.3 35/36 correct, 0 wrong; Qwen3.8 27b 32/36 correct, 4 wrong (h02 wrong department head, h06 tenure miscounted to 26 days, h18 count 6 instead of 5, e06 Io orbits 4 instead of 2 per Europa orbit). Pipeline arm (CodingAgent GLM over the ingested memory): 0/7 before the preregistered stop, because ingested fact symbols had no entity wires with labels, so the KnowledgeLinker asked 'Which entity do you mean by Galileo?'; plus 2 invalid circuits. Fix implemented: an entity-labelling stage (lib/ingest labelStage, CLI label-entities); not yet run to completion. The handbook memory also cannot answer tenure questions (calendar arithmetic not expressible; start dates stored as symbols). Conclusion so far: on short documents an LLM reading the text beats this ingestion pipeline; the pipeline's value has to come from long documents, auditability and small models, which this run did not reach. E-procedures not measured. Stopped by the coordinator: per-chunk omp drafting is too slow (4-16 min per chunk with thinking); a direct-LLM ingestion path replaces it.

author: claude-ingest-direct
title: Direct ingestion author: timings, accuracy, tiny vs small
body: Direct author (tier small) replaces omp per chunk. Wall: handbook 3 chunks 13.5 min (omp 42 min); per chunk 4-9 min dominated by 5k-token answers at ~30 tok/s plus patch repairs; 8000-token answers were lost to the 300 s fetch/header timeout, now capped at 5000 and continued. openference answers sometimes end early with finish stop and no usage: treated as interrupted and continued. Pipeline accuracy (correct/wrong/unknown of 18): handbook 4/1/13, europa 5/0/13; original europa memory after direct entity labels 6/3/9. Main blockers are not the author speed: dates as symbols (no tenure arithmetic), predicate drift between chunks (rules vs facts), an ambiguous label (Europa moon vs Europa the woman) making the linker ask, and 8 formalizer failures (reported to the formalization-errors inbox). tiny (Qwen3-4B, 8192 ctx) cannot take the ~10.5k-token prompt: futility stop.

author: analysis-procedures-agent
title: Analysis procedures: procedures in memory over a document layer; (a) 27/27, (b) limited by ingestion v2
body: Owner request 2026-10-03. Representation: a procedure wire tagged analysis (members = integrity/rule/aggregate/fact; findings = violations of its integrity members; measures = its report lines, new field P-8; parameters = analysis_parameter member facts, overridable). The analyzer (lib/analysis) builds a document view from the oracle's closure of the document layer (asserted_atom, denied_atom, keyed_value), runs each query through the StrategyRouter and explains every row with the oracle, so each finding has the rule, the proof and the document's quotes. Report wording: conversation-v1 line_* replies. Library analysis-core-v1: contradictions, numeric and temporal consistency, claim support, KPIs, a rubric.\n\nEvaluation on eval/analysis-v1 (8 own documents): (a) hand-written SOP 27/27 found, 0 spurious, 23/23 KPIs, 8/8 rubric scores (written with the procedures: coverage, not generality); (b) end to end through ingestion v2 on 4 documents: 2/15 found, 4 spurious, all quotes verified, then stopped. Causes are in the ingestion: unit-named document predicates instead of amount/upper_limit, no key declarations, statements about a whole distributed to its parts by the group repair, negations as separate predicates, a general statement stored as a fact. Suggestion for ingestion v2: offer and prefer the memory's analysis vocabulary; rerun (b) on all 8 when it does.

author: ingest-v2-agent
title: Ingestion v2 on eval-ingest-v1: does not beat v1 (handbook 1/2/15, Europa 4/5/9 vs v1 2/1/15, 5/4/9 on the same path)
body:
Ingestion v2 (lib/ingest/v2, template ingest-document version v2) measured on eval-ingest-v1, 18 questions per document, answered through the product question path (step-by-step formalizer on the product ladder tiny/small/good, proxy response cache off). Scorer: tools/eval/ingest-v1.mjs score (correct/wrong/unknown).

| memory | handbook | Europa |
|---|---|---|
| v1 baseline of 2026-10-02 (tier small only) | 4/1/13 | 5/0/13 |
| v1 memories, same path as v2 (2026-10-03) | 2/1/15 | 5/4/9 |
| v2 build 1 (final code before the group fix) | 3/2/13 | 1/2/15 |
| v2 build 2 (last; group findings from tables only) | 1/2/15 | 4/5/9 |

Verdict: v2 does NOT beat v1; v1 stays the template default. The single-tier small path of the baseline now fails intermittently (budget_exhausted at 8 tokens; cut answers were also replayed from the response cache), so both memories were measured on the product ladder.

Where the last run fails (31 non-correct): question formalization 14 (h01 h02 h05 h06 h07 h10 h12 h16 h17 h18 e03 e05 e06 e13: wrong predicate chosen, a spurious second conjunct, no join or arithmetic although the facts and rules are stored); vocabulary 5 (h09 h15 negative predicate names eligible/ineligible_for_overtime, no_receipt_required_below; e01 flyby count reified as amount(close_flybys_count, 12); e04 events named closest_approach not tied to Voyager; e09 depth only as limits); conversion/FOL 5 (h03 h11 exception and requirement written as facts of a group name; e07 e11 facts written as rules with a stray condition; e08 thickness in miles); missing knowledge 6 (h08 no zero-day statement for contractors, h13 no renewal-date rule, h14 thresholds as group facts, e12 no 'closest' ordering, e14 the 2019 date not stored, e18 surface age not stored); scorer 1 (e16: an honest 'no relation' answer to a not-stated gold is scored wrong).

Cost and time: each build 6.75-18 openference credits and 9-40 min wall time (medium FOL calls with reasoning, 10-20k output tokens each, plus queueing behind other agents); about 125 credits over 12 builds and probes on 2026-10-03. The last builds: handbook 10.5 credits, 664 s; Europa 6.75 credits, 557 s (14 cached calls; uncached 17.7 credits, 1495 s).

What works: canonical vocabulary (roster facts and rules share department_of, contract_type_of), dates as YYYYMMDD with exact calendar arithmetic, tenure derived by months_between, exceptions as defaults, closed table predicates, quotes and provenance on every wire, zero validator drops in the last builds. What does not: the FOL role's output varies run to run (group facts, units, negative names) and the question path does not reach knowledge that is stored. Next steps worth doing before another build: question-path fixes (predicate choice, spurious conjuncts) measured against the v1 and v2 memories offline; a deterministic lint of negative predicate names and group facts that feeds the repair; percent/units normalisation of shared relations.
